clauses.title: Prohibited practices: emotion recognition
clauses.text: The placing on the market or use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions shall be prohibited, except for medical or safety reasons.

clauses.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
clauses.text: AI systems referred to in Annex III shall be considered to be high-risk.

clauses.title: Annex III 4(a): Employment, recruitment
clauses.text: AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons, in particular to place targeted job advertisements, to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates.

clauses.title: Data governance: examination of biases
clauses.text: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be subject to examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect health and safety or lead to discrimination.

clauses.title: Technical documentation
clauses.text: The technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market and shall be kept up-to-date.

clauses.title: Annex IV: Technical documentation contents
clauses.text: General description, detailed description of elements and development process, monitoring, functioning and control, risk management system, changes, standards applied.

clauses.title: Record-keeping: automatic logging
clauses.text: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.

clauses.title: Automatically generated logs
clauses.text: Providers shall keep the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months.

clauses.title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
clauses.text: High-risk AI systems shall be designed to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret output and use it appropriately.

clauses.title: Instructions for use: performance characteristics
clauses.text: Instructions for use shall contain the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance of the high-risk AI system.

clauses.title: Human oversight: override
clauses.text: Natural persons to whom human oversight is assigned shall be enabled to decide not to use the system or to disregard, override or reverse its output.

clauses.title: Human oversight: stop
clauses.text: Natural persons shall be enabled to intervene in the operation of the system or interrupt it through a stop button or a similar procedure.

clauses.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
clauses.text: High-risk AI systems shall achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity.

clauses.title: Declared accuracy metrics
clauses.text: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.

clauses.title: Resilience against attacks
clauses.text: Technical solutions shall include measures to prevent, detect, respond to and control for data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples and confidentiality attacks.

clauses.title: Transparency: interaction with AI
clauses.text: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed so that the persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system.

clauses.title: Transparency: marking synthetic content
clauses.text: Providers of AI systems generating synthetic text, audio, image or video content shall ensure that the outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated.

requirements.title: No emotion recognition in workplace context
requirements.statement: The system does not infer emotions of candidates or employees from biometric or behavioural signals.

requirements.title: Risk class documented and justified
requirements.statement: The repository documents the AI Act risk class of the system with an explicit justification referencing Art. 6 / Annex III.
requirements.llm_guidance: Check whether the document states a risk class and justifies it against Annex III use cases.

requirements.title: Training data examined for bias
requirements.statement: Training/validation data sets are examined for biases affecting protected groups, with documented metrics and mitigations.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for bias/fairness analysis (demographic parity, equal opportunity) in notebooks, model cards or eval scripts.

requirements.title: Annex IV technical documentation
requirements.statement: Technical documentation covering the Annex IV sections (system description, development process, monitoring, risk management) is maintained in the repository.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compare docs against the Annex IV section list; report missing sections as gaps.

requirements.title: Automatic logging of AI decisions
requirements.statement: The system automatically records events (inputs, outputs, timestamps) for each model decision.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for logging of model inputs/outputs with timestamps for every prediction.

requirements.title: Logs retained for at least six months
requirements.statement: Automatically generated logs are retained for at least 180 days.
requirements.llm_guidance: Find the configured retention of decision logs and compare with 180 days.

requirements.title: Instructions for use for deployers
requirements.statement: Deployers receive instructions for use describing capabilities, limitations and how to interpret the system's output.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for user/deployer facing docs describing output interpretation and limitations.

requirements.title: Users informed they interact with an AI
requirements.statement: Natural persons interacting with a conversational interface are informed they are interacting with an AI system.
requirements.llm_guidance: Disclosure must be shown before or at the start of the interaction.

requirements.title: Machine-readable marking of generated content
requirements.statement: Generated text outputs are marked as AI-generated in a machine-readable form (metadata or watermark).
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for response metadata flags, headers or content credentials indicating AI generation.

requirements.title: Human reviewer can override AI output
requirements.statement: A human reviewer can disregard, override or reverse every automated decision before it takes effect.
requirements.llm_guidance: Check that rejection decisions are routed to a human, not only borderline scores.

requirements.title: Ability to interrupt the system
requirements.statement: Operators can halt automated processing via a stop mechanism (kill switch / feature flag).

requirements.title: Accuracy metrics declared
requirements.statement: Accuracy metrics and their values on a held-out test set are declared in the model documentation.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for metrics tables (precision/recall/AUC) in model cards or eval reports.

requirements.title: Resilience against adversarial input
requirements.statement: The system implements controls against adversarial or manipulated inputs (e.g. prompt injection in CVs, poisoned training data).
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for input sanitisation of uploaded documents and data validation in the training pipeline.

clauses.title: Data minimisation
clauses.text: Personal data shall be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed.

clauses.title: Storage limitation
clauses.text: Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed.

clauses.title: Information to be provided to the data subject
clauses.text: The controller shall provide the data subject with the identity of the controller, the purposes of processing, the legal basis and the recipients of the data.

clauses.title: Automated decision-making safeguards
clauses.text: The controller shall implement suitable measures to safeguard the data subject's rights, at least the right to obtain human intervention, to express their point of view and to contest the decision.

clauses.title: Security of processing: encryption
clauses.text: The controller and processor shall implement appropriate technical measures, including the pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data.

clauses.title: Data protection impact assessment
clauses.text: Where processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall carry out an assessment of the impact of the processing operations.

requirements.title: PII minimised before third-party processing
requirements.statement: Personal data is redacted or minimised before being sent to third-party model providers.
requirements.llm_guidance: Check the code path that calls the external LLM API for redaction of names, emails, phone numbers.

requirements.title: Personal data deleted after retention period
requirements.statement: Personal data is automatically deleted or anonymised after a defined retention period.
requirements.llm_guidance: Verify that every store of personal data has a retention/deletion mechanism.

requirements.title: Privacy notice shown at collection
requirements.statement: Data subjects are shown a privacy notice (controller, purposes, legal basis, recipients) when their data is collected.

requirements.title: Right to human intervention and to contest
requirements.statement: Data subjects subject to automated decisions can request human intervention and contest the decision.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for an appeal / contest flow exposed to candidates.

requirements.title: Encryption of personal data at rest
requirements.statement: Storage holding personal data is encrypted at rest.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.statement: A DPIA covering the automated processing is present and up to date.

clauses.title: No hard-coded secrets
clauses.text: Credentials, API keys and tokens must never be committed to source control; they are injected at runtime from the secret manager.

clauses.title: Model card required
clauses.text: Every production model ships with a model card describing intended use, training data, evaluation results and known limitations.

clauses.title: No PII in prompt logs
clauses.text: Prompt and completion logs must redact personal data before being persisted or shipped to observability tooling.

requirements.title: No hard-coded secrets
requirements.statement: No API keys, passwords or tokens are committed to the repository.

requirements.title: Model card present
requirements.statement: A model card is present for every production model.

requirements.title: Prompt logs redact PII
requirements.statement: Prompt/completion logs redact personal data before persistence.
requirements.llm_guidance: Check the logging middleware around LLM calls for redaction.
